title: Choose the visual world for the promo page
question: The roll assigned Marker Post. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Marker Post
options.lineage: yellow gas pipeline marker posts and numbered kilometre plates along a transmission line
options.thesis: The page walks the pipeline: every border is a numbered yellow post carrying its operator and its cost.
options.viewport: Headline stencilled on a tall yellow post at left; the route BG > RS > HU runs right as numbered posts with their EUR/MWh, ending at 3.6957; Open the calculator is the post's plate.
options.risk: Reads as a building-site hazard sign if yellow turns into warning stripes instead of plates.

raised.raise: Border points are numbered 1 to 4 in a strict margin column, one step per post.
Yellow is reserved for what matters now, the route total and the action; the rest is black on enamel.
Every figure sits in fixed tabular cells that align from post to post.
One stroke weight everywhere: posts, plates and the route line share it.
The saving is set as two halves: with quarters 3.6957 against without 3.9913.

options.label: Capacity Map
options.lineage: the ENTSOG transmission capacity map poster traders pin on the wall
options.thesis: The page is the network map, with the chosen route lit and priced point by point.
options.viewport: A wide schematic map of the 15 countries fills the screen; the BG > RS > HU route is lit with its costs; headline and button sit in the legend box.
options.risk: The most familiar direction for an energy tool, and it can look like the operators' own map.

options.label: Price Totem
options.lineage: seven-segment price totems at the roadside
options.thesis: The route cost glows like a fuel price board: 3.6957 in lit segments over ghost cells.
options.viewport: A totem stacks the three answers as lit readouts: EUR/MWh, EUR plus HUF, the guarantee; headline and action on the totem panel.
options.case: Fuses well: traders read prices off boards daily and the output is a price; loses on audience identification to the pipeline itself.
options.risk: Turns into a gas-station gimmick if segments spread beyond the numbers.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: The calculator as a text-mode board.
options.viewport: Title art over numbered menu lines.
options.case: Fuses poorly: traders and strangers do not identify with a BBS, and it hides the numbers.
options.kept: Figures in fixed cells on one grid.

options.label: Glazier Partition
options.thesis: Each answer is a pane; one lights up.
options.viewport: A wall of panes, the route total backlit.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to gas or routes.
options.kept: One saturated colour reserved for what matters now.

options.label: Crane Sequence
options.thesis: The route folds step by step.
options.viewport: A red sheet with numbered folds.
options.case: Fuses poorly: borrowed culture, no audience tie.
options.kept: Numbered steps in a strict margin column.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.thesis: The tariffs as an annotated edition.
options.viewport: Two dense columns round a keyed rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too bookish for a promo page; strangers stall.

options.label: Fight Poster
options.thesis: Quarters versus months, on the bill.
options.viewport: Two prices collide at a VS mark.
options.case: Fuses poorly: only the saving fits the form.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean software landing page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and button on the left, a screenshot of the map tab on the right, three feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other tool page by design.
